correctness.rationale: The exact jump response follows from the rank-M dyadic conditional expectation and orthonormal additional Rademacher times first-r Paley characters. A one-variable quadratic gives the exact maximum 1/(4N). The BV derivative-measure integral and Minkowski extend the bound to all real BV. Equality forces derivative support on finitely many optimal locations, and distinct residuals have incompatible non-grid jumps, so all extremizers are single jumps. Endpoints and N=1 are included. 1,658 exact rational finite checks corroborate but do not prove the infinite result.

originality.rationale: No covering joint-tail all-N Walsh approximation theorem was found in actual targeted comparisons. Fine (1949) establishes dyadic projection averaging and single-mode BV coefficient estimates, but neither its individual coefficient bound nor dyadic special cases imply the exact sharp non-dyadic residual identity, constant, and full extremizers. Moricz (1989) concerns variation of coefficient sequences; Vyas/Darji (2016) bounds multiple individual coefficients; Hytönen/Lacey/Parissis (2012) studies variation-norm Carleson sums. The unrestricted implication is not asserted merely from unmatched titles: their stated conclusions have different quantified norms and cannot supply the exact N-dependent equality formula. A classical unindexed equivalent remains possible.
residual_risks: Historically unindexed or untranslated classical Walsh approximation results might contain the same exact joint BV-to-L2 norm. No universal priority certificate is asserted.
Gogoladze–Tsagareishvili (2013) full text was inaccessible, so exact absence from that paper cannot be certified; the abstract addresses coefficient estimates rather than an all-N joint tail.
The contextual arXiv variational Carleson paper was assessed from its abstract and theorem scope, not its complete full text; it was not relied on for a whole-document NOT_COVERING claim.

value.rationale: The natural finite-rank Paley Walsh spectral approximation problem has a complete all-integer sharp constant and exact location classification, including non-dyadic cutoffs whose kernels are not local cell averages. Equality with N-equal-cell averaging at every rank is a structural and potentially useful benchmark for digitized discontinuous signals, not an arbitrary finite parameter slice. Individual coefficient bounds and dyadic-only estimates do not determine the non-dyadic joint error.
